lead: Text and buttons cover only part of a screen. Android adds a second family of views for pictures, progress and scrolling. ImageView and ImageButton draw bitmaps; WebView draws a web page; ProgressBar, SeekBar and RatingBar show and collect a value along a range; ScrollView, HorizontalScrollView and GridView move content that is bigger than the screen. Each of these has one rule that decides how its content is measured and scaled, and marks are lost when that rule is confused. Only a few universities teach this group in detail.
prereq: You need the basic views and the adapter idea from 3.4, and the view tree from 3.1.

blocks.text: An ImageView shows a drawable, usually a PNG or WebP file in res/drawable. Two XML attributes look alike but do different jobs. android:src is the image content, and it obeys scaleType. android:background paints the view's own background behind everything, and it is always stretched to the view bounds, ignoring scaleType.
scaleType decides how the source bitmap is fitted into the view box (view width W, view height H, bitmap width w, bitmap height h):

items: fitCenter: scale = min(W/w, H/h); the whole image fits, blank space is left over.
centerCrop: scale = max(W/w, H/h); the box is filled, the extra image is cropped.
fitXY: image is stretched to W × H, aspect ratio is not kept.
center: no scaling, image centred, cropped if larger than the box.
centerInside: scale down to fit, never enlarge, then centre.
matrix: you supply the scale and translation yourself.

blocks.text: android:adjustViewBounds="true" lets the view resize itself to the image's aspect ratio when one side is wrap_content. ImageView is used for product thumbnails, profile photos and map pins drawn over a layout.
ImageButton is an ImageView you can tap. It has android:src for the picture and no text. Use it for a search glass or a camera icon.

GridView lays children in a scrolling two-dimensional grid. It holds no data itself; like ListView it asks an adapter for each cell. Extend BaseAdapter and override getCount, getItem, getItemId and getView. getView receives a recycled convertView; set every field inside it on every call. Set android:numColumns to fix the number of columns.

items: Write the cell layout XML with one ImageView and one TextView.
Subclass BaseAdapter; return data.size() from getCount.
In getView, inflate the cell when convertView is null, otherwise reuse it.
Fill the ImageView and TextView from the data at the given position, then return the view.

blocks.text: WebView renders HTML inside your app. Call webView.loadUrl("https://example.com"). For network pages add <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET"/> to the manifest, otherwise the page fails with a blank screen.

ProgressBar shows work in progress. In determinate mode, with style="?android:attr/progressBarStyleHorizontal", call setProgress(n) where n runs from 0 to the maximum. Without that style it is indeterminate: a spinning circle with no value, correct when you cannot estimate the remaining time.

SeekBar is a slider. Attach a SeekBar.OnSeekBarChangeListener, which has three callbacks: onProgressChanged(seekBar, progress, fromUser), onStartTrackingTouch and onStopTrackingTouch. RatingBar shows stars: setNumStars(5), setRating(3.5f), and setStepSize(0.5f) for half stars.

ScrollView scrolls vertically and HorizontalScrollView scrolls sideways. Each holds exactly one child, so put a LinearLayout inside it and add the rest to that layout. A GridView scrolls by itself and must never sit inside a ScrollView. VideoView plays a video file in one line of code; playback itself belongs to another unit.

figure.caption: Same 400×300 px view, same 200×600 px bitmap, two scaleTypes. fitCenter shrinks the bitmap to 100×300 px and leaves 150 px blank on each side; centerCrop enlarges it to 400×1200 px and cuts 450 px from the top and from the bottom.

spec.title: Worked example: view 400×300 px, bitmap 200×600 px
spec.aria: A worked example branching from one 400×300 px view with a 200×600 px bitmap into fitCenter, which draws 100×300 px with 150 px blank on each side, and centerCrop, which draws 400×1200 px and crops 450 px top and bottom.

examples.question: An ImageView is 400 px wide and 300 px high. The source bitmap is 200 px wide and 600 px high. Find the drawn size of the bitmap and the amount cropped or left blank for scaleType fitCenter, and then for centerCrop.
steps: fitCenter uses scale = min(W/w, H/h) = min(400/200, 300/600) = min(2, 0.5) = 0.5.
Drawn width = w × 0.5 = 200 × 0.5 = 100 px; drawn height = h × 0.5 = 600 × 0.5 = 300 px.
The image fits the height exactly, so no height is lost. The blank width is 400 − 100 = 300 px, split as 300/2 = 150 px on the left and 150 px on the right.
centerCrop uses scale = max(W/w, H/h) = max(2, 0.5) = 2.
Drawn width = 200 × 2 = 400 px; drawn height = 600 × 2 = 1200 px.
The width fills the box exactly. The height is cropped from 1200 px to 300 px, so 1200 − 300 = 900 px is lost, 900/2 = 450 px from the top and 450 px from the bottom.
examples.answer: fitCenter draws the bitmap at 100 × 300 px with 150 px blank on each side; centerCrop draws it at 400 × 1200 px and crops 450 px from the top and 450 px from the bottom.
examples.check:
W, H = 400, 300
w, h = 200, 600
fit = min(W / w, H / h)
print(w * fit)
print(h * fit)
print((W - w * fit) / 2)
crop = max(W / w, H / h)
print(w * crop)
print(h * crop)
print(h * crop - H)
print((h * crop - H) / 2)

examples.question: A 600 × 400 px ImageView holds a 300 × 300 px bitmap. Find the drawn size for fitCenter and for centerCrop.
steps: fitCenter: scale = min(2, 1.333) = 1.333, drawn 400 × 400 px, blank height 400 − 400 = 0, blank width 600 − 400 = 200 px, 100 px each side.
centerCrop: scale = max(2, 1.333) = 2, drawn 600 × 600 px, crop height 600 − 400 = 200 px, 100 px from the top and 100 px from the bottom.
examples.answer: fitCenter draws 400 × 400 px with 100 px blank on each side; centerCrop draws 600 × 600 px and crops 100 px top and bottom.
examples.check:
W, H = 600, 400
w, h = 300, 300
fit = min(W / w, H / h)
print(w * fit)
print(h * fit)
print((W - w * fit) / 2)
crop = max(W / w, H / h)
print(w * crop)
print(h * crop)
print((h * crop - H) / 2)

traps: fitXY stretches the bitmap to the view box and drops the aspect ratio, so faces look fat; it is the answer examiners expect to be marked wrong.
scaleType acts on src only. A background drawable is stretched to the view bounds and ignores scaleType completely.
fitCenter and centerInside differ when the bitmap is smaller than the view: centerInside never enlarges, fitCenter does.
A ScrollView with two direct children crashes at inflation; wrap them in one layout.
GridView needs an adapter and recycles row views, so getView must set every field on every call or old images reappear.

quiz.q: Which ImageView attribute holds the image content, and which holds the background?
quiz.a: android:src holds the content; android:background holds the background, which is stretched to the view bounds.

quiz.q: Why does fitXY make a photo look distorted?
quiz.a: It scales width and height independently to the view box, so the aspect ratio of the bitmap changes.

quiz.q: A 300 × 500 px ImageView shows a 100 × 100 px bitmap with centerCrop. Give the drawn size and the crop.
quiz.a: scale = max(3, 5) = 5, drawn 500 × 500 px, width cropped from 500 to 300, so 100 px lost at each side.

quiz.q: Same view and bitmap with fitCenter. Give the drawn size and the blank space.
quiz.a: scale = min(3, 5) = 3, drawn 300 × 300 px, blank height 500 − 300 = 200 px, 100 px above and 100 px below.

quiz.q: How many direct children may a ScrollView have, and what do you do when the screen needs five widgets?
quiz.a: Exactly one; put a LinearLayout inside the ScrollView and add the five widgets to that layout.

quiz.q: Which permission does a WebView need to load a network page?
A GridView shows the wrong picture in some cells after the user scrolls. Explain the likely cause.
quiz.a: getView reuses convertView; if a branch fails to set the ImageView on every call, the recycled cell keeps an old image. Set all fields on every call.

beyond: Not for the exam. In production Android, plain ImageView is usually replaced by image-loading libraries that download, cache and downscale bitmaps off the main thread, because a full-size photo in an ImageView causes jank and out-of-memory crashes. WebView grows into a full app shell with JavaScript bridges and custom clients. Progress and rating views feed design systems that fix colours and sizes once. Search next for bitmap memory reuse, image loading caches, and WebView security settings.
